item.title: Social media erupts after DeSantis gives ‘Soros’ protester a piece of his mind: ‘Ain’t my first rodeo’
item.description: Ron DeSantis fired back at a heckler he accused of being paid by George Soros during a Florida GOP event, telling her "this ain't my first rodeo."
item.content:encoded:
Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis set social media aflame Tuesday night after he did not hold back in his response to a disruption by a woman he accused of being paid by George Soros, yelling back at her that "this ain’t my first rodeo."

DeSantis was touting Florida’s economy at a state GOP campaign event in Tampa when he was interrupted mid-sentence by a heckler. The governor did not hesitate in his response.

"Hey, Soros isn't paying you enough because you're not very good at this," he said, pointing to the woman as security personnel approached her in the crowd.

"You should try again," DeSantis continued as the crowd booed the heckler. Keeping with the Soros line, DeSantis piled on, "He needs to pay some better talent instead of having people like you show up. This ain't my first rodeo, lady. I've seen it all, and you ain't very good at it."

BYRON DONALDS SHUTS DOWN BILL MAHER’S CLAIM ON GOP PRIMARY RACISM, SAYS 'FLORIDA IS A MERITOCRACY'

After another heckler interrupted the event again that same evening, DeSantis shot back, "Let me just give you guys some advice: standing up and screaming is not effective. Okay?"

"I've seen people try to do this over the years," he continued. "Some are more effective than others."

"I remember I had Antifa charge me, and one of our FDLE [Florida Department of Law Enforcement] leveled them, and it was funny, and it was good."

"But here's the deal," he leaned in. "I think Soros is tightening his wallet because the people he's paying are terrible at this."

SOROS PROSECUTOR IN DANGER OF BEING REMOVED AFTER GRIEVING MOM’S DESPERATE ALARM: ‘CAN’T BELIEVE THIS’

"He used to hire people who were really good. Now they're just screeching, and it's almost like, I don't even know what it is. And so, listen, you should be respectful, you should listen. This is part of the civic process," he said. "But, if you're not going to do that, do a better job at protesting, please. Gosh."

"THAT'S MY GOVERNOR!!" reacted conservative commentator Eric Daugherty on X, writing, "DeSantis just PUMMELED a leftist heckler who disrupted his speech tonight."

Another popular conservative influencer who simply goes by the name Greg reacted, "Soros protester is re-thinking opening her mouth at the RPOF [Republican Party of Florida] Event. DeSantis with the takedown."

Another X account, DeSantis Appreciation Society, wrote, "The Tribal Chief @RonDeSantis just bodied a Soros protester into next week at the RPOF event."

"DeSantis is a legend. Absolutely obliterated a liberal heckler, lol. Best governor ever!" wrote another popular conservative account going by the name "American Nightmare."

ANTIFA-LINKED SITES GO DARK AFTER STATE DEPARTMENT TERROR DESIGNATION OF TECH COLLECTIVE

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

In response, a spokesperson for the Soros family’s philanthropic group, the Open Society Foundations, directed Fox News Digital to a 2025 statement that said, "We do not pay people to protest or directly train or coordinate protestors."

While the statement called nonviolent public protests "hallmarks of any vibrant society," the group said that "All Open Society grantees are required to comply with the law and we expect our grantees to uphold our shared commitment to human rights, dignity, and nonviolence."

Under the Florida Constitution, DeSantis, who is serving his second consecutive term, is not eligible to seek another consecutive term as governor this year. During Tuesday's event, he endorsed a statewide slate of Republicans, including GOP gubernatorial nominee U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds.

The event showcased Donalds as well as other Republican candidates, Attorney General James Uthmeier, Florida Chief Financial Officer Blaise Ingoglia and Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson.

item.title: Raiders name Kirk Cousins as Week 1 starting quarterback, Fernando Mendoza will begin career as backup
item.description: The Las Vegas Raiders named Kirk Cousins the team's starting quarterback on Wednesday, meaning No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza will begin his career as a backup.
item.content:encoded:
Mendoza-Mania will not be coming to Las Vegas just yet.

Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak announced Wednesday that the team is naming Kirk Cousins its Week 1 starting quarterback against the Miami Dolphins, meaning Fernando Mendoza will begin his career as a backup.

"(Cousins has) played really good football, I’m really happy with all three of (the) quarterbacks. Kirk’s had a really good offseason, very good camp, and he’s earned it," Kubiak told reporters.

When asked if he expects Mendoza to play at all this year, Kubiak deflected the question and said the team is focused on the Dolphins.

Raiders general manager John Spytek and minority owner Tom Brady have been advocates about letting a rookie develop behind a veteran quarterback, which makes the team's decision to roll with Cousins unsurprising.

Spytek said Mendoza has shown the team everything it learned about him in the draft process when talking to reporters Tuesday.

"He’s a tireless worker. He loves football. He loves his teammates. He’s energetic on the field. He’s self-critical. He’s self-aware. He’s very accurate," Spytek said during a recent press conference. "His time is coming, but he’s got to earn it every day, and he knows that. I think we’re all very pleased with the person and his work ethic and his commitment to being a great quarterback."

When asked if the team has a proof of concept for how to best develop a young quarterback, Spytek cited examples from multiple different processes.

"Tom Brady, Aaron Rodgers, Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, but Jayden Daniels. Like you said, there’s success stories and failures in both ways," Spytek said. "We’re just trying to build the best team we can and play the guys that are most ready to play, and have a constant competition in every room, not just the quarterback room, but every room."

Brady, Rodgers, Love and Mahomes all sat during their rookie years and, in some cases, multiple seasons before taking over starting jobs and flourishing. Daniels, however, started as a rookie and thrived, winning The Associated Press NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year and making the Pro Bowl after leading the Commanders to the NFC championship game.

Kubiak said Brady has been a great resource for the team when it comes to making the decision on the team's starting quarterback.

Cousins signed a two-year deal with the Raiders in the offseason after being released by the Atlanta Falcons following a tumultuous two seasons.

Cousins was benched in Week 15 in 2024, the first year of the deal, for rookie Michael Penix Jr. after the four-time Pro Bowler struggled down the stretch as he battled through injury. Cousins started eight games last season, including the final seven after Penix tore his ACL, and the team had a 5-3 record in his starts, including winning the last four.

In 10 games and eight starts last season, Cousins completed 61.7% of his passes for 1,721 yards with 10 touchdowns and five interceptions. The veteran quarterback has the 19th-most regular-season passing yards (44,700) and 15th-most passing touchdowns (298) in NFL history.

Cousins also had familiarity with Kubiak from their time with the Minnesota Vikings. They spent three seasons together, with Kubiak serving as Cousins’ quarterbacks coach for two seasons and offensive coordinator for another in Minnesota.

Cousins will hope that familiarity will pay off when the Raiders play the Dolphins in Week 1.

item.title: Alabama AG Marshall fires back at USPS mail-ballot order critics: ‘This is about securing elections’
item.description: Steve Marshall says Democratic AGs are blocking voter roll audits to obstruct Trump's election integrity executive order ahead of the midterms.
item.content:encoded:
Republican Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall argues that his Democratic counterparts do not care about election integrity in the same way Republicans do, as they attempt to block measures designed to root out illegal voters they have long claimed do not exist.

Marshall addressed a legal challenge brought by 25 Democratic state attorneys general challenging President Donald Trump's executive order that included provisions for federal agencies to help states ensure only citizens receive mail-in ballots, and for the U.S. Postal Service to institute practices to make the ballots trackable.

"The left, because they’re concerned about losing at the midterms, want to be able to obstruct this administration’s efforts to ensure the integrity of our elections," Marshall told Fox News Digital this week, ahead of Thursday's oral arguments before U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani in Boston.

"You have to wonder – when those that are objecting to this – how confident they can be in the security of their elections, as opposed to becoming just a partisan opportunity to ensure the Democrats win and keep conservative voices from being heard, not only in local and state levels of government, but particularly in Washington."

DHS PLANS COSTLY CRACKDOWN ON STATES THAT DON’T COOPERATE ON ELECTION SECURITY

Marshall led a letter in July from 13 Republican attorneys general, backing the U.S. Postal Service's following up on Trump's March 31 executive order that set up an audit of states' voter rolls.

"There shouldn't be a reason why we object to that, but yet Democrats simply don't want to have fair elections in a way that people can have confidence," Marshall claimed.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Democratic Attorneys General Association for comment on Marshall's remarks, but they did not immediately respond.

Democrats, in various arguments to block the audit of voter rolls before the mailing out of absentee ballots, claim that it would lead to "disenfranchisement," "chaos," "unconstitutional overreach" and a partisan "power grab."

Democrats' concern is that if they refuse to share their voter rolls with the Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration to crosscheck the eligibility of legal voters, the USPS can stop the mailing of state's absentee ballots.

"USPS's interest in correcting an unsubstantiated problem through likely unconstitutional means is dwarfed by the overwhelming risk of pervasive disenfranchisement of citizens who need access to mail ballots in order to vote," Talwani, appointed by former President Barack Obama, wrote in her restraining order against the Trump administration.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION FROM RESTRICTING MAIL-IN BALLOTS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS

"The postal service is not a partisan organization. As the postmaster said, I think most recently, we're just there to deliver the mail. They're experts in how it is that this can be configured."

Marshall stated that the problem of voter fraud is documented, not "unsubstantiated," as Talwani put it, with evidence in his own state.

USPS WOULDN'T DELIVER BALLOTS IN STATES THAT REFUSE TO FORK OVER MAIL-IN VOTER INFO UNDER PROPOSED RULE

"This is not a solution looking for a problem," he said. "This is in response to what we know is going on across the country. And this provides a commonsense, straightforward way for states to be able to ensure elections, but most importantly, for the people of this country to have belief that their elections in fact are accurate."

MAIL-VOTING CRACKDOWN MOVES AHEAD AS TRUMP COURT WIN OPENS DOOR TO FEDERAL ACTION

"It's not a shock that Democrats are standing up the ability for us to pass the SAVE [America] Act because they don't want to allow for there to be assurances of what is already in the law: That somebody here illegally cannot be able to vote," he added. "But here we have the president being able to make sure that we are allowing for government resources to be used in an appropriate way to simply allow those who are qualified to vote, vote, and those who aren't, don't."

Marshall has little confidence that the Obama-appointed judge in Boston is going to side with the Trump administration and the law.

"I would be remiss if I didn't say that I would fully expect her to continue with the Democratic Party line," he said. "The Trump administration has already filed a request with the First Circuit to try to get a stay of that order, but yet we're going to continue to battle this case along with the administration and look forward to standing beside them when they obtain this victory."

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS

Marshall maintains Republicans are not stopping anyone from getting an absentee ballot – they're just trying to make sure the process is conducted legally and securely.

"Here we have a barcode that allows us to be able to connect it directly with the voter – we have the assurance that that ballot is being cast by the person in fact that receives that ballot," he said. "Democrats and Republicans alike ought to praise this as a commonsense effort to be able to restore election integrity in this area, but it's not a shock that Democrats have opposed it."

MORE THAN A QUARTER-MILLION NONCITIZENS MAY BE REGISTERED TO VOTE IN 4 KEY STATES, DHS ALLEGES

Marhall pointed to the 2005 bipartisan commission chaired by former President Jimmy Carter and former Secretary of State James Baker that identified mailed absentee ballots as being susceptible to fraud.

"This is about securing elections, not interfering with states' abilities to conduct elections, and we think that we'll be able to eliminate many of the issues that we've seen, including in Alabama, that have occurred in the past."

The restraining order Talwani issued will remain in place for up to one more week while she considers whether to issue a longer-term preliminary injunction blocking the rule. The hearing is Thursday in Boston, but the fight will go on from states on both sides as the midterm mail-in ballot season officially gets underway.

item.title: Thai resort city cracks down on prostitution ahead of USS Abraham Lincoln arrival
item.description: Pattaya police ramped up patrols and raids ahead of the USS Abraham Lincoln's arrival, arresting over 50 people as 5,000 sailors hit the resort city.
item.content:encoded:
A Thai resort city began cracking down on prostitution ahead of the arrival of 5,000 U.S. sailors and Marines exhausted from months at sea in the Middle East.

The USS Abraham Lincoln docked near Pattaya, one of Thailand's primary nightlife areas, on Wednesday along with two other naval vessels, The Independent reported.

"We are doing our best, but it is difficult," Pattaya police chief Anek Srathongyoo said Monday of his department's efforts to curb prostitution in the city.

TRUMP PRAISES OUSTED NAVY SECRETARY PHELAN AMID TENSIONS WITH PENTAGON LEADERSHIP

The police effort involves increased patrols in beachfront and nightlife areas, as well as raids over the weekend in which more than 50 people were arrested on suspicion of prostitution.

Although prostitution is illegal in Thailand, major tourist hubs like Bangkok and Pattaya are well known for sex tourism.

The San Diego–based USS Abraham Lincoln left port in November and was redirected to the Middle East amid the U.S. war with Iran.

However, the prolonged deployment raised concerns amid reports of health issues, deteriorating conditions aboard the warship, and low morale.

US STOPS 9 OIL TANKERS ATTEMPTING TO BREAK TRUMP'S BLOCKADE ON IRANIAN PORTS

Pattaya Mayor Poramase Ngampiches expressed hope that the influx of American service members would boost the region's economy.

Each service member could spend around $30 to $90 per day, depending on where they stay and for how long, the mayor said.

"When we heard the news that a U.S. Navy warship would be docking in Pattaya, it became a source of hope for us," said Lisa Hamilton, president of the Pattaya Nightlife Business Association.

Pattaya originally grew from a small fishing village into a major tourism hub largely due to U.S. military members seeking rest and relaxation during the Vietnam War.

item.title: Florida police learn the hard way to not trust 'Crooked Jess' with money to buy crack for undercover operation
item.description: Jessica Straubel Sanchez, aka "Crooked Jess," allegedly vanished with $60 given by an undercover officer to buy crack cocaine in Pinellas County.
item.content:encoded:
I'd like to think there's one officer that attended the meeting where an undercover drug bust was being discussed that raised a concern about using a person with an alias of "Crooked Jess" to buy the drugs.

I give a tip of the cap to that officer. The rest of the officers at the Pinellas County Sheriff's Office who were part of setting this undercover operation up and didn’t listen owe the officer an apology.

Back in March, "Crooked Jess" aka Jessica Straubel Sanchez made off with $60 she was given to purchase crack cocaine and disappeared, according to an arrest affidavit.

DITCHING HIS 'WHIZZINATOR' IN A PATROL CAR WAS FLORIDA MAN'S SECOND BAD DECISION OF DAY

Police finally caught up with the 41-year-old and arrested her on Saturday, reports The Smoking Gun. The undercover officer explained that Straubel was supposed to return with crack cocaine after being given $60 to buy it.

The officer watched as she walked over to the residence and went into the backyard. After an hour, which the officer pointed out is "more than a reasonable amount of time to wait for a narcotics transaction to occur between two subjects," she failed to return.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK CULTURE COVERAGE

"Crooked Jess" had allegedly lived up to her name. She was nowhere to be found after officers drove around the area and came up empty. They also had no way of getting in touch with her because she "did not own a phone."

It was determined after a short search for her that she "had no intentions of coming back to facilitate the transaction and had deprived me of my money for her own use."

A truly shocking twist to the otherwise foolproof undercover operation meant to score some illicit narcotics from a known residence known for facilitating such activity.

TSG reports that along with the theft, "Crooked Jess" was charged with possession of drug paraphernalia. An officer had allegedly found fentanyl residue on some foil she had tucked away "within the defendant's undergarments."

As you may have guessed, this wasn't her first run-in with the police. She's had others. Call me a dreamer if you must, but my hope is that she hasn't been part of her last undercover drug bust. I'd like to see "Crooked Jess" be given a second chance here to make things right.

item.title: Platner's replacement faces new Senate campaign headache tied to his son's lobbying
item.description: Former State Senator Troy Jackson backed millions in public funds for Maine Maritime Academy while his son was a registered lobbyist for the school.
item.content:encoded:
Former state Senator Troy Jackson, who has replaced Graham Platner as the Democratic Senate nominee in Maine, backed bills seeking to send millions of dollars in public funds to a college while his son lobbied on its behalf, documents show.

Jackson’s son, Chace, was registered as a lobbyist for the Maine Maritime Academy at the same time as his father was serving as president of the Maine Senate, according to state lobbying records. In 2024, the elder Jackson co-sponsored legislation that would have sent $13.4 million to the maritime academy after pushing a bill providing the institution with an additional $2 million per year in 2023, with both pieces of legislation being drafted while Jackson's son was lobbying for the college.

"Troy Jackson authored Augusta’s failed status quo and has turned public office into a family affair of self-enrichment," National Republican Senatorial Committee press secretary Bernadette Breslin told Fox News Digital. "He’ll always prioritize personal kickbacks over the needs of working Mainers."

5 THINGS TO KNOW ABOUT GRAHAM PLATNER ALLY POISED TO TAKE ON SUSAN COLLINS

Before his son was lobbying on its behalf, Jackson also supported legislation in early 2022 that provided the academy with a one-time $6.8 million payment to fund repairs to one of its buildings.

Jackson’s son first registered as a lobbyist for the Maine Maritime Academy in December 2022, according to public records. He renewed his lobbying registration in January 2024, just as his father was co-sponsoring legislation that would have sent over $10 million to the academy.

While the Maine Maritime Academy funding boost Jackson backed in 2023 went into effect, his 2024 bill passed the Maine Senate but was never signed into law.

"Troy Jackson has fought for working Mainers, and [is] guided by one goal: fixing our broken system so Maine's working families stop getting squeezed while the rich get richer," a spokesperson for the Jackson campaign told the Washington Free Beacon, which first reported on the lobbying records.

LIKELY PLATNER REPLACEMENT'S RESURFACED POSTS ON 'DEMOCRACY' COME BACK TO BITE HIM: 'HYPOCRITICAL SOCIALIST'

In April, Jackson justified his failed run for governor by claiming that the "status quo isn't working" in Maine because of "special interests, high-priced lobbyists and corporate greed." In addition to representing the Maine Maritime Academy, Chace Jackson works as one of the expensive lobbyists his father has criticized, at one point representing the multinational alcohol company behind premium beverages such as Johnnie Walker whiskey and Don Julio tequila.

In 2024, while his father was the Maine Senate president, the younger Jackson represented nine clients. That sum dropped to five clients after his father left the chamber in 2025.

AFTER PLATNER IMPLOSION, MAINE DEMOCRATS RUSH TOWARD NEW SENATE NOMINEE DESPITE FRESH WARNING SIGNS

A bill targeting an oil and gas giant died in the Maine Senate during Jackson's Maine Senate tenure and while his son was lobbying on behalf of the fossil fuel corporation in question.

The former state senator is facing off against incumbent GOP Sen. Susan Collins in November. Jackson replaced Platner as the Democrat on the ballot after his campaign was hit with a series of controversies, ranging from crude deleted Reddit posts to a Nazi-linked tattoo, which culminated in an allegation of rape, prompting the self-identified oyster farmer to drop out of the race.

Jackson, his son and the Maine Maritime Academy did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

item.title: NFL to commemorate 25th anniversary of 9/11 terrorist attacks across all its stadiums and even in Australia
item.description: The NFL will stencil "Never Forget" in every end zone and auction special 9/11 tribute coins as all Week 1 games mark the terror attacks' 25th anniversary.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes the NFL does the right thing. And the league's intention to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks so that its fans do not forget what happened is one such instance.

America's most popular league and its 32 clubs will honor the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001, through a series of commemorative efforts in communities across the globe.

"We continue to honor the memory of those we lost on September 11 and the heroes whose courage and sacrifice inspired our nation," NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement on Wednesday. "Out of unimaginable tragedy emerged an extraordinary sense of unity and service that brought Americans together.

9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS

"As the NFL family reflects on this day 25 years later, we remember those who were taken from us and support those who continue to carry the pain of that day. We also recommit ourselves to the spirit of resilience, community, and service that remains an enduring example for future generations."

The NFL says all Week 1 games will feature tributes designed to honor the lives lost, recognize survivors, first responders and military families, and connect fans to the lasting message of remembrance and service that emerged after September 11.

FOX NATION, TUNNEL TO TOWERS EXPLORES HOW AMERICA’S PASTIME HELPED A GRIEVING NEW YORK HEAL AFTER 9/11

NFL clubs will participate through in-stadium moments, broadcast integrations – including live national anthem coverage across 1 p.m. ET games – and community engagement efforts throughout the week.

OutKick first reported over the weekend that the league will have clubs stencil "Never Forget" in stadium end zones the first week of the season. And, yes, those will go away after Week 1 and be replaced by other messaging.

Game officials will use special 9/11 tribute-branded coins for the pregame toss. Those coins will later be auctioned on the NFL Auction platform to benefit the league’s September 11 charitable partners.

When the New York Giants host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, mere miles from where the Twin Towers were attacked by Muslim terrorists who flew planes into the building, players, coaches and staff from both teams will wear commemorative NYPD, FDNY and PAPD hats on the sideline in recognition of the first responders who served and died on 9/11 and in the days that followed.

Players and coaches from both teams will also wear special 9/11-branded "Never Forget" T-shirts during pregame warmups. Giants-branded versions of the caps will be available for purchase at the team store, with proceeds benefiting the respective agencies.

The NFL is even taking its 9/11 ceremonies abroad.

During the NFL’s first-ever regular season game in Australia, pregame ceremonies will honor the 25th anniversary of 9/11 with U.S. and Australian color guards and large-field flag presentations featuring U.S. Marines, Navy personnel and Australian service members.

Through its Salute to Service partnership with TAPS, the NFL Foundation will also support weeklong activities for military families of the fallen with a connection to 9/11, including a ceremony at Melbourne’s Shrine of Remembrance and on-field recognition before the game.

The NFL says it is doing all this to "honor those affected by the tragedy and reaffirm its commitment to preserving the lessons and legacy of that day for years to come."

item.title: Rescuers use ziplines to transport trapped citizens after devastating Nepal floods decimate country's bridges
item.description: Video shows rescue workers using cable cars and ziplines to ferry stranded citizens across flooded rivers in Nepal after the deadly mudslide.
item.content:encoded:
Rescue workers in Nepal were forced to use cable cars and ziplines to ferry stranded citizens across rivers after August's deadly flood and mudslide wiped out local bridges.

Video shows teams of workers yanking ropes to ferry locals who were stranded on an embankment flanked by a flooded river. In one clip, a pair of people sit in a small box attached to a wire as they're yanked onto a platform across a river in Nuwakot, Nepal.

The rescues come as both Nepal and neighboring China continue to deal with the aftermath of the Aug. 26 mudslide and ensuing floods in Tibet's Gyirong Valley and the Nepal's Trishuli River Valley.

EXPERTS ZERO IN ON LIKELY CAUSE OF DEADLY NEPAL MUDSLIDE, WITH MORE THAN 1,400 MISSING

As of Wednesday, at least 1,114 people have been confirmed dead and nearly 4,000 remain missing in Nepal. Chinese authorities report an additional 16 confirmed dead and at least 541 missing on their side of the border.

Rescuers are still working to search and rescue any potential survivors trapped in a hydropower tunnel in the Rasuwa district.

ROUGHLY 80 AMERICANS STILL UNACCOUNTED FOR AFTER HIMALAYAN DISASTER KILLS 903, OFFICIALS SAY

"In Rasuwagadhi, we think 46 people are trapped in a room-like structure in the tunnel," Amshu Kiran Shahi, a board member of the Nepal Electricity Authority that operates the hydropower plant, told Reuters.

A senior official in President Donald Trump's administration also told Fox News that an additional two Americans made it to safety in Nepal, marking 16 total Americans in the country who made their way to safety.

SON REALIZES MISSING AMERICAN DAD WAS IN PATH OF NEPAL DISASTER AFTER WATCHING VIRAL VIDEO

Seventy-five Americans in Nepal currently remain unaccounted for while no American casualties have been reported so far.

Fox News Digital contacted the U.S. State Department and Nepal's Foreign Ministry for further comment.

Fox News' Gillian Turner and Reuters contributed to this report.

The Georgetown County Sheriff’s Office said John Herb Hayes III, 70, and Geordyn Nichole Hayes, 31, were arrested Tuesday evening in Tennessee and booked into the Carter County Jail on fugitive-from-justice charges.

The couple is accused of putting their daughter in danger or abandoning her under South Carolina law.

The couple will be transported back to South Carolina once extradition proceedings are completed. Carter County jail records show both were booked Tuesday evening.

Arrest warrants issued in Georgetown County describe Saylor as severely nonverbal and autistic, with a strong attraction to water and a history of wandering away from her caregivers.

After Saylor was discovered missing, the warrants allege that the Hayeses directed search efforts toward tracking technology despite knowing she was not wearing the device. The couple also allegedly directed search efforts away from the nearby body of water.

Among them is veteran character actor Nick Searcy, who has a lot to say about his departure from the Golden State.

‘TWILIGHT’ STAR KELLAN LUTZ TRADED CALIFORNIA FOR TENNESSEE LAND AND BIBLE STUDIES

Searcy, who moved to Los Angeles in the early ’90s, became a Hollywood character actor, known for his role in the popular TV series "Justified," as well as film roles in 1993’s "The Fugitive," 2000's "Cast Away," 2003’s "Runaway Jury" and, more recently, 2024’s "Reagan" and Netflix’s "The Perfect Couple," which was also released that year.

The actor, an outspoken conservative, told Fox News Digital that in the early ’90s, LA was still a wonderful place to work.

"I’m old enough to remember when Hollywood was this beautiful, kind of inaccessible place that, you know, if you were really good at acting, you could some day move to. That’s how I grew up," Searcy recalled.

"There was a lot of activity. I had 15 auditions a week during pilot season… but then it started to go downhill. They started to centralize more and more of the Democrat power base, and they just systematically took that city down," he continued.

NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE'

As the years went on, Searcy said he increasingly worked outside Los Angeles, including in Oklahoma, Toronto, Atlanta, the Dominican Republic and London.

"It was like, I would never shoot anything in Los Angeles," he said. And he said to his wife, "Why are we here? Why are we still here paying all these taxes?"

KEVIN SORBO SAYS HE ‘ESCAPED’ CALIFORNIA, SLAMS DEMOCRATIC LEADERSHIP IN FIERY REMARKS

The last straw for Searcy was when COVID hit.

"We realized that it wasn’t just the government that was crazy, it was all of our neighbors," Searcy quipped. "They were wanting to put us in jail for not wearing our mask over our nose or not getting vaccinated. And that’s when my wife turns to me and says, ‘Yeah, we got to go.’"

CALIFORNIANS FLEEING TO RED STATES ARE DRIVING UP HOME PRICES AND RENTS IN THEIR NEW CITIES, DATA SHOWS

Like many others before him, Searcy, a North Carolina native, and his wife, a Kentucky native, relocated their family to Nashville in 2021. Searcy said they now split their time between Music City and a small town in Kentucky.

"… It was a logical place for us to land with family near and a lot of my friends from California were here already," he said. "A lot more people have come since then. It’s pretty crowded."

'HERCULES' STAR KEVIN SORBO SAYS CALIFORNIA CAN KEEP ITS TAXES, TRAFFIC AND 'NEGATIVITY': 'I'M DONE'

While many celebrities have left California, some have maintained homes in the state while making another state their primary residence.

Yet even that’s changing.

JOE ROGAN MOCKS GAVIN NEWSOM FOR DISMISSING GROWING STATE PROBLEMS AS LA FILM PRODUCTION CRATERS

Actor Dennis Quaid, who moved to Nashville in 2020, only recently moved from his Brentwood Hills home after decades of building his career in LA.

Quaid has noted the community he’s built in Nashville and how LA once had that back in the day when actors attended auditions in person. Since then, the industry has evolved into a place where auditions are primarily done online.

TRUMP, SCHIFF FORGE UNLIKELY ALLIANCE AS HOLLYWOOD BLEEDS JOBS

Besides Tennessee, others have cut ties and left for Florida, Nevada, Texas and beyond.

Searcy said that 20 years ago, he couldn’t have imagined what has happened to the iconic City of Angels.

"The city’s been destroyed, and I think it’s deliberate," Searcy said. "I think they’re deliberately making it impossible to live there so that all the sensible people move away. That way, the political class stays in power because the only people that are left there believe their nonsense."

"I don’t see how anybody stays there," he continued. "So many people have left. It makes sense for the industry to move because the people that kept it afloat, the sort of people — the talents that they were basing a business on — they’ve all moved out. So it makes perfect sense for the studios to start taking advantage of the fact that there are better, more economically viable places to run your business."

He even thinks a possible move by Paramount to Nashville, as rumored, isn’t a bad idea.

"I think it’s the best thing that could possibly happen," Searcy said. "I think the film business has left California anyway. It’s time for the industry to start finding its footing elsewhere because shooting there is just impossible. Unless you’re Netflix or Amazon and have all the money in the world, California is not the place to be anymore."

item.title: Dale 'Grey Beard' Sanders reclaims title as oldest person to thru-hike the Appalachian Trail at 91
item.description: Dale "Grey Beard" Sanders reclaimed his own Appalachian Trail age record at 91, surviving 71 falls across 2,200 miles to summit Mount Katahdin.
item.content:encoded:
In case you were feeling particularly productive and accomplished today, a man named Dale "Grey Beard" Sanders is about to humble you.

At 91-years-old, Sanders officially reclaimed his title Monday as the oldest person ever to complete a thru-hike of the Appalachian Trail, finishing his journey atop Mount Katahdin in Maine.

And before we go any further, understand that hiking the Appalachian Trail is an extraordinary feat for any hiker — let alone someone with nine decades under his belt.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The AT stretches roughly 2,200 miles from Springer Mountain in Georgia to Katahdin in Maine, crossing 14 states along the way. According to the Appalachian Trail Conservancy, hikers who complete the whole thing experience about 464,500 feet of elevation gain— and an equal amount of loss.

That combined 929,000 feet of elevation change is equal to going from sea level to the top of Mount Everest and back roughly 16 times.

And here I was proud of myself for taking the stairs at the airport.

The distance alone is obviously absurd, but mileage is only part of what makes the AT such a beast.

Unlike some long-distance trails that offer extended stretches of relatively forgiving terrain, the AT spends much of its length going relentlessly up and down the Appalachian Mountains. Hikers contend with steep climbs, boulder fields, exposed roots, mud, stream crossings and rocks upon rocks upon rocks.

CLIMBING EL CAPITAN WHILE NEARLY BLIND: WHY EITAN ARMON REFUSED TO SIT AROUND WAITING FOR A CURE

Then you reach New Hampshire's White Mountains and Maine, where the trail gets particularly rude.

Southern Maine and the Whites are considered among the most difficult portions of the AT, with steep ascents and descents and rugged terrain. And before hikers can officially call themselves finishers on a northbound journey, they still have to deal with Katahdin — a mountain that requires more than 4,000 feet of climbing and stretches of scrambling over boulders and ledges.

Consider that the grand finale. And Sanders did it at 91 years old.

According to the Associated Press, he fell just 200 yards from the finish. It was his 71st fall of the journey. Six of those were what Sanders considered "hard falls," including one that eventually resulted in a brief hospitalization.

Here’s where the story gets crazier.

Sanders didn't just break the Appalachian Trail age record. He reclaimed his own record.

Back in 2017, Grey Beard completed the trail at age 82, becoming the oldest person to do it at the time. His record stood until 2021, when his friend M.J. "Nimblewill Nomad" Eberhart finished at 83.

14 TAILGATING ESSENTIALS FOR GRILLING, WATCHING THE GAME AND STAYING WARM

Sanders actually helped Eberhart during that record-setting hike, joining his friend for some difficult stretches when Eberhart was considering quitting.

But then, Sanders decided he wanted his title back.

He started this latest attempt from Harpers Ferry, West Virginia, on Sept. 6, 2025, hiking south toward Georgia before taking the winter off. He returned in the spring and headed north from Harpers Ferry toward Maine, targeting about 12 miles per day with one rest day each week. The Appalachian Trail Conservancy allows thru-hikers to complete sections in different orders and take breaks, provided the entire trail is completed within a year.

Sanders finished in 359 days.

Fun fact: Sanders was born in 1935. The Appalachian Trail wasn't completed until 1937.

The man is literally older than the trail he just hiked.

Sanders has spent his later years collecting endurance accomplishments that would exhaust most people half his age. He has paddled the entire Mississippi River — more than once — and became the oldest person to complete the trip when he did it at 87. He's also set an age record on the Grand Canyon's grueling rim-to-rim-to-rim route.

Still, this Appalachian Trail attempt wasn't easy even by Grey Beard standards.

During a June descent of Vermont's Killington Mountain, Sanders went down in a boulder field hard enough to bloody his arms and legs. Weeks later, numbness in his left arm sent him to a hospital, where what was initially feared to be a stroke turned out to be a pinched nerve. He briefly considered abandoning the attempt before eventually returning to finish the job.

So, fellow adventurers, the next time you're 20 minutes into a hike, staring at a switchback and wondering whether you really need to see what's at the top, just remember Grey Beard.

Because if a 91-year-old man can hike the entire Appalachian Trail, we're officially out of excuses.

item.title: Trump revives Iran regime change speculation with cryptic call for people to ‘rise up'
item.description: Trump asking when Iranians will “rise up and fight" revives questions over whether the administration’s Iran strategy is shifting beyond economic pressure and negotiations
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump revived speculation over regime change in Iran Tuesday night, openly asking when Iranians would "rise up and fight" as his administration intensified military and economic pressure on a government US officials say is increasingly vulnerable.

"I'm not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table," Trump wrote on Truth Social Tuesday. "I like our position now much better, with almost total control of the Hormuz Strait, and their economy totally collapsing."

"They are just playing out the inevitable," Trump added. "When are the Iranian people going to rise up and fight?"

IRAN REGIME CHANGE TALK RESURFACES AS TRUMP SAYS TEHRAN 'WANTS TO MEET' AMID US STRIKES

Trump did not explicitly call for the overthrow of Iran's government, and the White House has not publicly announced a policy of U.S.-led regime change. But his appeal to the Iranian population comes as the administration increasingly portrays Tehran as approaching an internal breaking point. Fox News Digital reached out to the White House for clarification Wednesday. 

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described Iran as being in a "death spiral" during remarks Monday, arguing that economic pressure was rapidly narrowing the government's options.

"They are panicked. They are resorting to kinetic because they are getting squeezed economically," Bessent said told Ed Lawrence on Fox Business.

COULD IRAN’S REGIME COLLAPSE? EXPERTS ASSESS BESSENT’S BID TO SEVER FINANCIAL LIFELINES

Bessent said Iran could eventually face one of three outcomes: "Either the IRGC are going to turn on each other, the people are going to turn on them, or they are going to come to the table and want to do a deal that they can stick with."

"They are in the death throes," he added, comparing Iran's deterioration to bankruptcy occurring "slowly, then quickly."

Miad Maleki, a senior fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies and former Treasury sanctions official, told Fox News Digital that Washington does not need to choose between invading Iran to overthrow the government and striking another agreement with Tehran.

"It's very clear U.S. government is not in the business of regime change anymore," Maleki said. "And I think it's very clear that we're not going to have boots on the ground to invade Iran. And I don't think we need that."

INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE'

Instead, Maleki argued Washington should "contain this regime, cut off its economic lifelines, empower the Iranian people" and prepare for another wave of demonstrations inside Iran.

"We need to be prepared to support the Iranian people in a way that they can be empowered and take the government back," he said, stressing the importance of ensuring protesters maintain access to the internet so they can communicate, mobilize and make their voices heard.

Maleki described Iran's leadership as the weakest it has been since the 1979 Islamic Revolution and argued that further Iranian military escalation could deepen its vulnerability rather than restore lost leverage.

The debate comes as reports of localized economic protests continue to emerge from inside Iran.

TRUMP SAYS IRAN IS ‘DEAD’ — EXPERTS POINT TO THE REAL SIGN TEHRAN IS NEARING THE BRINK

The National Council of Resistance of Iran, an exiled Iranian opposition coalition, said Tuesday that workers, retirees, drivers and job-seeking young people demonstrated in several cities on Aug. 31. The group alleged security forces opened fire on job seekers in Gachsaran and Ahvaz and reported separate demonstrations over unpaid wages, inflation, fuel shortages and working conditions. Those specific claims have not been independently verified by Fox News Digital.

Iran analyst Benny Sabti also told Fox News Digital that deteriorating living conditions could become a catalyst for broader unrest. "People are hungry," Sabti said, predicting Iranians would "take the streets again."

"Hunger is humiliating," he said, arguing that economic desperation could eventually outweigh fear of the government's security apparatus.

The political stakes are rising alongside a dramatic military escalation. US forces carried out another wave of strikes Tuesday against Iranian air-defense systems, radar installations, maritime assets and mine-laying capabilities, according to US Central Command, while Iran retaliated with missile and drone attacks against US assets across the region.

For Trump, however, Tuesday night's post suggested the question may no longer be only whether economic pressure brings Tehran back to negotiations — but what happens inside Iran if it does not.

item.title: Cybercrime losses near $21B: 5 ways to protect your money
item.description: The FBI reports nearly $21 billion in cybercrime losses for 2025, up 26%, as AI scams make fake voices and identities more convincing than ever.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly $21 billion. That number jumped out at me when I looked at the FBI's latest cybercrime data. Behind that enormous loss are families who watched savings disappear and people who trusted the wrong investment pitch. Some victims had no clue someone was moving their money until they checked an account.

Americans reported nearly $21 billion in losses to cyber-enabled crime during 2025, up 26% from the year before. Investment fraud caused the biggest financial hit at about $8.65 billion. I recently joined "Fox & Friends Weekend" to talk about those numbers and a bigger problem I see coming. Scammers now have AI tools that can make a fake message, voice or identity far more believable than the clumsy scams many of us learned to recognize years ago. That changes how we need to protect our money.

Here are five practical steps you can take now to put stronger barriers between scammers and your savings.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Protect Your Money replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay and download our financial protection checklist. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five simple ways to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. You’ll learn how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed.

Get the free replay and checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com

IDENTITY THEFT LOSSES SURGE 70% FOR OLDER AMERICANS

For years, one of the standard pieces of scam advice was to look for obvious mistakes. Maybe an email had terrible grammar. Perhaps the caller sounded suspicious. AI can now erase many of those clues.

The FBI says its Internet Crime Complaint Center received 22,364 complaints in 2025 that included AI-related information. Reported losses tied to those complaints reached about $893 million. The FBI also warns that criminals can use AI to create fake social profiles, cloned voices and convincing videos.

That gives scammers another way to build trust before asking for money or personal information. So telling you to "be careful" no longer feels like enough advice to me. I want barriers between a scammer and your money.

You cannot predict every scam that may come your way. However, you can put safeguards in place that make it harder for a criminal to reach your money.

Start with your bank and credit cards. Open the official app or website for each financial institution and look for notification settings. Turn on alerts for transactions and transfers. You may also be able to receive warnings about suspicious account activity.

The exact choices vary by bank. However, the goal stays simple. If money moves and you did not authorize it, you want to know quickly. I have talked with victims who discovered fraud long after criminals gained access. A real-time alert gives you a chance to call the financial institution and react much sooner.

Next, check the security settings on your bank, credit card and investment accounts. Use a strong password that you do not reuse elsewhere, which a password manager can help you create and store. Then turn on two-factor or multifactor authentication (2FA) wherever your financial institution offers it.

If the company supports an authenticator app, passkey or another stronger verification method, consider using that option. Texted security codes still add protection, although your phone number can become a target in a SIM swap attack.

Also protect the email account connected to your finances. A criminal who controls your email may be able to reset passwords or intercept account notifications. For a closer look at the different login options, see Are bank text codes enough to protect you?

Your phone number has quietly become part of your financial security. In a SIM swap or port-out scam, a criminal tricks a carrier into moving your number to another SIM or device. Once that happens, calls and texted security codes can start going to the scammer.

Contact your carrier or check its account-security settings. Look for a number transfer lock, port-out protection or another feature designed to block unauthorized transfers. If your phone suddenly loses service for no clear reason, pay attention. Contact your carrier from another device, especially if you also notice unusual activity involving your financial accounts.

IDENTITY RESTORATION: WHAT TO DO AFTER IDENTITY THEFT

A credit freeze remains one of the strongest free tools available for preventing new-account fraud. You need to place a freeze separately with Equifax, Experian and TransUnion. Once active, the freeze restricts access to your credit file and makes it much harder for someone to open a new credit account using your identity.

A freeze does not hurt your credit score. You can also lift it when you legitimately need to apply for credit. One warning: go directly to the official credit bureau websites rather than clicking an ad or unfamiliar search result. Criminals know people search for credit-freeze help too. CyberGuy has step-by-step guidance on how to freeze your credit and clean up your online data at Cyberguy.com

This one worries me because retirement accounts can represent decades of someone's work. We recently covered a case involving a Colgate-Palmolive employee whose entire $751,430 401(k) was allegedly drained after an impostor changed the account's contact information. The case later settled on undisclosed terms.

Log in to your retirement and investment accounts and review their security settings. Make sure your contact information remains correct. Turn on account alerts and multifactor authentication. Then ask your brokerage or retirement-plan provider what protections it offers for withdrawals and transfers. Some providers offer additional verification or other controls that can make unauthorized transfers harder. This deserves the same attention you give your checking account. Maybe more.

If you want to go deeper than the steps above, I will walk through each one in more detail in my CyberGuy LIVE class, Protect Your Money From Today's Biggest Threats . The live event has ended, but the full replay and CyberGuy Money Protection checklist are available now.

In the class, I show you how to put these protections in place step by step, including where to look for bank alerts, how to strengthen account logins, ways to lock down your phone number, how to freeze your credit and what to ask your retirement or investment provider about added safeguards. You can pause the replay and work through each step at your own pace.

Watch the free CyberGuy LIVE replay and get the Money Protection checklist at CyberGuyLive.com

YOUR BANK MAY STOP TEXTING YOU SIX-DIGIT CODES

What worries me about the FBI's nearly $21 billion figure goes beyond the size of the number. Scammers have become better at taking advantage of moments when people naturally trust what they see or hear. AI raises the stakes because a familiar voice or polished message can create a false sense of confidence. The FBI's numbers show how much money is already disappearing through cyber-enabled crime. I would rather see you build protections now than depend on spotting one tiny clue in the middle of a convincing scam. Turn on the alerts and secure the accounts holding your money. Then look at the protections surrounding your phone number, credit and retirement savings. Cybercriminals only need one good opportunity. Your job is to make that opportunity much harder to find.

Have you ever received a scam call, email or investment pitch that was so convincing you almost believed it? What finally tipped you off? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

item.title: SMU cancels CAIR-Texas youth conference over state’s ‘terrorist’ designation of organizer
item.description: Southern Methodist University canceled a CAIR-Texas youth leadership symposium after Greg Abbott designated CAIR as a foreign terrorist organization.
item.content:encoded:
Southern Methodist University has canceled an "Unapologetically Muslim" youth conference organized by CAIR-Texas that was scheduled to bring high school and college students to its Dallas campus, citing Texas’ designation of the Council on American-Islamic Relations as a "foreign terrorist" organization.

The Sept. 19 conference was advertised as a day of leadership and civic engagement training featuring "interactive sessions," "mock testimony" and "power mapping," a community-organizing technique aimed at identifying and influencing people with decision-making power.

The event page on the website for CAIR-Texas says that the event is "designed for high school students and rising college freshmen and sophomores" and that "students will hear from community leaders and professionals, take part in interactive workshops, and learn how they can get more involved in the issues affecting their communities."

BACKLASH ERUPTS OVER VIRAL VIDEO OF CAIR LEADER AS NEWSOM FUNDING DRAWS SCRUTINY

On Friday, The Dallas Morning News reported that SMU had canceled the event citing Gov. Greg Abbott’s designation of the Muslim Brotherhood and the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) as foreign terrorist organizations and transnational criminal organizations.

"The Muslim Brotherhood and CAIR have long made their goals clear: to forcibly impose Sharia law and establish Islam’s ‘mastership of the world,’" Abbott said in a November statement.

DEMS IN THE HOT SEAT FOR SKIPPING CRUCIAL HEARING ON RADICAL GROUP HIDING IN US: 'EMBARRASSMENT'

"The actions taken by the Muslim Brotherhood and CAIR to support terrorism across the globe and subvert our laws through violence, intimidation, and harassment are unacceptable," he said.

Abbott added, "These radical extremists are not welcome in our state and are now prohibited from acquiring any real property interest in Texas." The designation by the governor is a state designation and not a federal one. 

In November 2025, CAIR sued Abbott and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton to block the proclamation.

"This attempt to punish the nation’s largest Muslim civil rights and advocacy organization simply because Governor Abbott disagrees with its views is not only contrary to the United States Constitution, but finds no support in any Texas law," the group said in its lawsuit.

"CAIR-Texas and the Texas Muslim community are standing up for our constitutional rights by directly confronting Greg Abbott’s lawless attack on our civil rights," CAIR-Texas said in a statement. "We are not and will not be intimidated by smear campaigns launched by Israel First politicians like Mr. Abbott. Mr. Abbott is defaming us and other American Muslims because we are effective advocates for justice here and abroad. We plan to continue exercising our constitutional rights, defending civil rights, and speaking truth to power, whether in defense of free speech, religious freedom and racial equality here in Texas or in defense of human rights abroad."

The federal lawsuit remains ongoing.

The Houston Chapter of CAIR-Texas was started in 1994, according to its website. 

The group's website lists its core principles as supporting Islam, fostering equality, stimulating interfaith dialogue and condemning violence.

The group says it works to "promote a positive image of Islam and Muslims in America," with efforts that include media relations, government relations, education, and advocacy "to ensure the Muslim voice is represented."

HARVARD REPORTEDLY INVESTIGATING REPUBLICAN CLUB OVER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ABOUT MUSLIM GROUP'S CAMPUS EVENT

In a statement to Fox News Digital on Tuesday, a spokesperson at SMU confirmed the event had been canceled.

"SMU welcomes a wide range of organizations and perspectives to campus as part of our commitment to open inquiry and the free exchange of ideas," the spokesperson said. "After reviewing plans for an upcoming unaffiliated youth leadership symposium advertised to take place at SMU, the University has determined that permitting the event to take place on campus, given the State of Texas’ current designation of the symposium’s organizer, is inconsistent with our mission and related University policies. As a result, the event will not take place on campus."

Fox News Digital reached out to CAIR-Texas for comment.

– Fox News' Landon Mion contributed to this report.

Robert Carey, the lawyer for Mayich’s family, is searching for answers as the player remained incapacitated from an Aug. 20 on-campus workout. The session began in the morning of Aug. 20 as classes for the first semester of school were just about to get underway.

item.title: Tyler Robinson defense attorney should be ‘embarrassed’ for attacking Charlie Kirk as full of hate: lawyer
item.description: Tyler Robinson's defense attorney called Charlie Kirk hateful in court, drawing sharp rebukes as the Kirk family watched during the preliminary hearing.
item.content:encoded:
PROVO, Utah — A lawyer for the accused Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson drew rebukes inside and outside the courtroom Tuesday over remarks that painted the victim as the one behaving "hatefully" before he was shot and killed in front of thousands of people during a public speaking event at Utah Valley University.

"I think what the defense attorney said regarding Charlie Kirk and that he was full of hate, that was so unprofessional," said David Gelman, a New Jersey-based criminal defense attorney who has been following the case. "That was so out of left field that he honestly — he should be embarrassed of what he said."

Robinson, 23, is accused of assassinating the 31-year-old father of two at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, as Kirk was speaking in front of thousands of onlookers during a Turning Point USA event on campus.

TYLER ROBINSON HEARING COULD DECIDE DEATH PENALTY FATE, FINALLY SEE PLEA IN CHARLIE KIRK CASE

"Mr. Kirk spoke hatefully of certain groups of people," California-based defense attorney Richard Novak claimed during his argument against binding over the case for trial. He went on to say that there was a "significant gap" between what Kirk stood for and what Robinson felt about him.

WATCH: Charlie Kirk murder suspect Tyler Robinson to stand trial

As Novak repeated the phrase, Kirk's parents, widow and other relatives were in court. They exchanged looks and some teared up. Erika Kirk leaned forward and said something to an aide with the county attorney's office.

TYLER ROBINSON HEARING: TOP MOMENTS FROM EXPLOSIVE LANCE TWIGGS INTERVIEW PLAYED IN COURT

"You don't ever and I mean ever say that, No. 1, as a defense attorney or a prosecutor, especially not even at a trial," Gelman said. "If you want to paint Charlie as a bad person in front of the jury, knock your socks off. Do whatever you think you have to do. But to do that at a preliminary hearing...when you have the victim's family all there, that was totally uncalled for."

Chief Deputy Utah County Attorney Chad Grunander and Kirk family attorney Jeffrey Neiman both pushed back on Novak's comments in front of the judge.

item.title: Reported shooting at Virginia elementary school 'contained,' sheriff's office says

"All Westwood students, teachers, and staff are accounted for and are safe," Waynesboro Public Schools posted Wednesday morning on social media, adding that the school was reuniting students and families at a designated location during a temporary lockdown.

"I think the White House definitely should use the ballroom to be beautiful and nice. Because, I think that the president should be able to have fun and invite people to the ballroom," she said.

item.title: Why one detail about NFL final rosters proves former Florida coach Billy Napier was worse than you remember
item.description: The 4-8 Florida Gators produced nine players on NFL 53-man rosters, matching Alabama and Georgia despite Billy Napier's disastrous final season.
item.content:encoded:
All 32 NFL teams made their final cuts to trim their active rosters down to 53 men earlier this week, a sign that football is slowly but surely coming back into our lives.

With rosters being finalized, it also means we can see how many rookies ended up making it to the NFL, and all the usual suspects are well represented.

The Ohio State Buckeyes led the way with 11 rookies from the 2026 Draft class on NFL rosters, followed by Texas A&M, which had 10 former Aggies make it to the league.

Those two make sense, considering they dominate the recruiting rankings year in and year out and both made the College Football Playoff this past season.

Other mainstays like Alabama and Georgia were right behind the Aggies and Buckeyes with nine rookies on NFL rosters, but another team that hasn't even sniffed the CFP in the last several years was hilariously lumped in with the rest of these upper echelon college programs.

THE 5 MOST DISAPPOINTING PRESEASON TOP-10 COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS OF THE 21ST CENTURY

That's right, folks! The 4-8 Florida Gators produced a staggering nine players from their 2025 football team that ended up on 53-man rosters in the NFL.

Talk about doing less with more, right?

And yes, there are some qualifiers that need to be thrown out there about these players.

One is a long snapper, and while it's important to have a good long snapper, it doesn't exactly move the needle in the win-loss column.

The other is Caleb Banks who, while being a first-round pick, only played in three games for Florida in 2025.

But, when you couple that with the fact that a lot of Florida's best players weren't even draft eligible this past April - like All-SEC running back Jadan Baugh, Freshman All-SEC wideout Vernell Brown III, sack leader and Freshman All-SEC edge rusher Jayden Woods, and leading tackler/All-SEC linebacker Myles Graham - you start to see just how disappointing this team was this past season.

And it starts at the top.

Head coach Billy Napier took a team loaded with NFL talent and a five-star quarterback under center in DJ Lagway and led the Gators to the worst possible outcome.

Seriously, if you gave that Gators team an average coach and simulated the season 1,000 times, I don't think he would do worse than 4-8 unless his entire roster spontaneously combusted.

Florida's in-state rivals, the Miami Hurricanes, also had nine rookie players make an NFL roster this week, and that team played for a national championship just this past season in addition to embarrassing the Gators the two times they met up on the field in 2024 and 2025.

Asking this team to go out and win a national title might be a bridge too far, but Florida was a darkhorse Playoff contender this time a year ago.

And the Gators didn't even make a bowl game.

This is why Napier is no longer employed by the University of Florida, but it's a good reminder of why Gators athletic director Scott Stricklin probably should have pulled the trigger sooner.

While most of its peers with regard to roster talent were out here winning 10 games and making the CFP, Florida won a whopping two SEC games and lost to South Florida in The Swamp.

Think about that for a second.

How many USF Bulls do you see on NFL rosters this week?

I rest my case.

Florida's impressive NFL presence only highlights how incompetent the Napier regime was, but it's also a silver lining for Gator fans.

If new head coach Jon Sumrall and his staff are even competent coaches, supporters of the program won't have to endure rock bottom for too much longer.

Again, is it fair to expect a national championship right away?

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

No. But a seven or eight-win season and a nice bowl game would be a great start, which, ironically enough, represented Napier's ceiling.

Coaching matters, and if you want proof, look no further than the 2025 Florida Gators.

And after you're done looking, try not to run to your toilet and puke.
